body:
Aditya Rao: Need a quick decision on tier naming + customer-facing copy for the batching defaults. Internally we have `fast`, `standard`, `cost_efficient` but there’s been a suggestion to call cost-efficient “eco” in the Console/docs. Want to settle this today so DevEx + Console can ship stable strings.

Soojin Lee: From a messaging POV, “Eco” is shorter and feels friendlier, but it’s ambiguous (environmental vs cost). “Cost-efficient” is clear but long. Do we need the exact words to match the API param?

Henry Cho: Console dropdown has limited space but we can wrap. My concern with “eco” is it sounds like it’ll just be slower always; “cost-efficient” also implies slower but at least it says why.

Nikhil Sharma: Also API-wise we already have people asking for predictable naming. If docs say “eco” but config param is `cost_efficient`, support is going to get tickets.

Elliot Price: +1. Docs consistency matters. We can have a short label and a long description though. E.g. label “Cost-efficient” and then a one-liner under it.

Alex Martinez: SDK examples will show `batching_tier="cost_efficient"`. If Console says “Eco”, we’ll need extra callouts everywhere like “Eco (cost_efficient)” which is kinda gross.

Monica Patel: TypeScript typings too. If marketing name diverges, we’ll end up with two vocabularies. We’ve been burned by that in other settings.

Soojin Lee: Ok, but we still need something that reads well in the UI. “Cost-efficient” is a mouthful. What about “Cost Efficient” (no hyphen) for UI label and “cost_efficient” for the config value?

Henry Cho: That works. UI label: “Cost efficient”. Subtext: “Lowest $/token. Higher latency; not recommended for streaming.” Something like that.

Aditya Rao: That’s basically where I’m leaning: keep the tier name as “Cost-efficient” in customer-facing surfaces; reserve “eco” for internal shorthand (if at all).

Miguel Santos: (CS/SE) Please please keep it explicit. We already have confusion about “performance mode” vs “batching”. If it’s “Eco” we’ll spend half the call defining it.

Soojin Lee: Got it. Let’s align on the *exact* strings so docs/Console/Optimize tooltips match.

Aditya Rao: Proposed names + short descriptions:
- Fast — “Lowest latency. Best for interactive chat + streaming. Higher cost.”
- Standard — “Balanced latency and cost. Recommended default.”
- Cost-efficient — “Lowest cost per token. Higher tail latency; best for offline/batch workloads.”

Henry Cho: Suggest we avoid “offline” as the only use-case. Some folks will use it for non-streaming API routes in prod. Maybe: “Best for non-streaming and higher throughput workloads.”

Nikhil Sharma: +1. Also clarify that streaming *works* but token cadence may degrade. So “Not recommended for latency-sensitive streaming.”

Alex Martinez: Can we add a doc note: “If you need stable token cadence, use Fast.” That’s a common question.

Elliot Price: For docs, I want a consistent pattern:
Tier name (UI)
`batching_tier` value (code)
When to use
Trade-offs

Soojin Lee: Copy tweaks:
- Fast: “Prioritizes responsiveness and streaming cadence.”
- Standard: “Balances responsiveness and cost (recommended).”
- Cost-efficient: “Prioritizes throughput and unit cost; may increase queueing under bursty load.”

Henry Cho: “queueing” is a bit inside baseball for the UI. Maybe “may increase waiting under high load” for UI; keep queueing for docs.

Aditya Rao: Works. Also question: hyphenation. “Cost-efficient” vs “Cost efficient”.

Elliot Price: I’d do “Cost-efficient” in docs/marketing copy; “Cost efficient” in UI label if hyphen looks weird in dropdown. But consistency is better; most UIs can handle hyphen.

Monica Patel: Prefer “Cost-efficient” everywhere (title case in UI). It reads fine.

Soojin Lee: Agree. Let’s do “Cost-efficient” everywhere.

Nikhil Sharma: One more: do we call it “Cost-efficient” or “Cost Efficient”? (Title case). Console likely wants title case.

Henry Cho: Console dropdown entries will be Title Case: “Fast”, “Standard”, “Cost-efficient”.

Aditya Rao: ok.

Aditya Rao: Decision (unless strong objections in next 30m):
- Customer-facing tier names: Fast / Standard / Cost-efficient
- Config values remain: `fast`, `standard`, `cost_efficient`
- We will *not* use “eco” in Console/docs, only internal shorthand if needed.

Soojin Lee: :thumbsup: No objections.

Alex Martinez: :thumbsup: Will update SDK snippets to reflect these strings and add the note about streaming cadence.

Elliot Price: I’ll update docs plan + FAQ wording. Also adding a small callout: “Explicit batching overrides take precedence over tier defaults.” (CS keeps asking for that.)

Miguel Santos: Thank you. That single line will prevent 10 support threads.

Henry Cho: I’ll ping Console team with the exact labels + tooltip text. Proposed tooltip drafts:
- Fast: “Lowest latency and best streaming cadence. Higher cost.”
- Standard: “Balanced latency and cost. Recommended.”
- Cost-efficient: “Lower cost per token. Higher latency under load; avoid for latency-sensitive streaming.”

Nikhil Sharma: Looks good. Minor: “avoid” might be too absolute; maybe “not recommended”.

Henry Cho: Good call. Will change to “not recommended”.

Aditya Rao: Locking it. Thanks all. I’ll post this in the release notes draft too so we don’t re-litigate next week.

(reactions: Soojin Lee added :white_check_mark: to Aditya Rao’s decision message)
(reactions: Miguel Santos added :pray: to Elliot Price’s “explicit overrides” message)
